nodes.summary: The conditional upper-tail p-value of a statistic `T` of the allelic partition: the conditional probability, given the observed number of alleles `K(π)`, that `T` is at least its observed value `T π`. It is written with the cycle-type weights and so does not involve `θ` (by `ewensCondProb_eq` it is the conditional tail probability for every `θ > 0`).
nodes.title: Conditional upper-tail p-value of the Ewens–Watterson test

nodes.summary: The number of permutations of `n` letters with cycle type `π`, `w(π) = n! / ∏ j, j ^ (a j) * (a j)!` with `a j = π.parts.count j` (Cauchy's formula).
nodes.title: Number of permutations with a given cycle type

nodes.summary: The Ewens–Watterson conditional law (Ewens 1972; Watterson 1978): for `θ > 0`, `P(π | K = K(π)) = w(π) / |s(n, K(π))| = n! / (|s(n, k)| ∏ j, j ^ (a j) (a j)!)`.
nodes.title: The Ewens–Watterson conditional law

nodes.summary: `K` is sufficient for `θ` (Ewens 1972): for `θ > 0`, the conditional law of the allelic partition given the number of alleles is `w(π) / ∑_{K(π') = K(π)} w(π')`, which does not depend on `θ`.
nodes.title: `K` is sufficient for `θ`

nodes.summary: The conditional probability of the allelic partition `π` given that the number of alleles is `K = K(π) = π.parts.card`, under the Ewens sampling formula with parameter `θ`.
nodes.title: Ewens conditional probability given the number of alleles

nodes.summary: Factorization of the Ewens sampling formula (Ewens 1972): `P_θ(π) = θ ^ K(π) / θ^{(n)} * w(π)`, with `K(π) = π.parts.card` the number of alleles.
nodes.title: Factorization of the Ewens sampling formula

nodes.summary: The sample homozygosity `F(π) = ∑_i (n_i / n)²`, the sum over the alleles of the squared sample frequencies (Watterson 1978); `n_i` ranges over the parts of `π`.
nodes.title: Sample homozygosity of an allelic partition

nodes.summary: Law of the number of alleles (Ewens 1972): `P_θ(K = k) = |s(n, k)| θ ^ k / θ^{(n)}`. As an identity between the defining sums it holds for every real `θ`; it is a probability for `θ > 0`.
nodes.title: Law of the number of alleles

nodes.summary: The probability `P_θ(K = k)` that a sample of `n` genes carries exactly `k` distinct alleles under the Ewens sampling formula.
nodes.title: Probability of a given number of alleles under the Ewens formula

nodes.summary: For `θ > 0`, every number of alleles `k` and every level `t ≥ 0`, the conditional probability given `K = k` that the conditional upper-tail p-value of `T` is at most `t` is at most `t`.
nodes.title: Conditional validity of the Ewens–Watterson test

nodes.summary: Validity of the Ewens–Watterson test (Watterson 1978): for every `θ > 0` and every level `t ≥ 0`, the Ewens probability that the conditional upper-tail p-value of `T` is at most `t` is at most `t`. With `T = homozygosity` this is the test against excess homozygosity, with `T = -homozygosity` the test against a deficit of homozygosity.
nodes.title: Validity of the Ewens–Watterson test

nodes.summary: The cycle-type weights of the partitions of `n` into `k` parts sum to the unsigned Stirling number of the first kind `|s(n, k)|`.
nodes.title: Cauchy's count by number of cycles

nodes.summary: For nonnegative masses `q` on a finite set `s` and a statistic `T`, the upper-tail p-value `p x = ∑_{y ∈ s, T x ≤ T y} q y` satisfies `∑_{x ∈ s, p x ≤ t} q x ≤ t` for every `t ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Validity of a discrete upper-tail p-value

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
